changes.balance: The strip is not pricing a Joliet return. The front of the curve is pricing fall egress plus two broken PADD 2 demand binaries; the light-end dislocation is a coker-arbitrage story, not weak crude demand.
changes.body: The free ICE Report Center end-of-day PDFs yielded full settlements for Sep 29 on all six Canadian-differential futures, the first real strip prints in days (the public ICE product pages still publish no settlement tables). WCS at Hardisty (TMW): Nov26 -$22.10 (-$1.40 on the day), Dec26 -$22.55 (-$1.05), front-heaviest shape with December the widest point, tightening about $5 into summer 2027. WCS at Houston (ARV): Nov26 -$14.618 (-$2.368) — the Houston leg fell harder, collapsing the implied Hardisty-to-Houston arb to +$7.48. MSW (TMR) Nov26 -$0.75, nearly at parity; synthetic crude (TMS) Nov26 +$5.55 unchanged, so the SYN-minus-WCS spread is $27.65; UHC (TMU) +$5.10; condensate (TMF) Nov26 +$2.40, the only contract up on the day, firming into winter diluent season.
changes.conditional: Public Joliet confirmation → the front snaps tighter. No confirmation plus a weak EIA PADD 2 print → the strip has it right.
changes.delta: TMW Nov26 -$22.10 (-$1.40 d/d); ARV-TMW arb collapsed to +$7.48
changes.source: ICE Report Center end-of-day settlements, Sep 29, 2026
changes.title: The ICE strip returns — WCS front widens $1.40 on the supposed Joliet-return day

changes.balance: While Joliet is dark, the WCS discount stays pressured wide; a confirmed restart is the classic snap-tighter catalyst. Today's EIA weekly is the public test.
changes.body: ExxonMobil's Joliet, Illinois refinery (~275 kb/d) still has no public restart confirmation: the only 'back in service' reports remain paywalled Quantum Commodity Intelligence headlines (Sep 24/28), and ExxonMobil's last public word (Sep 18) said the refinery was restarting with no date. The market must assume roughly 275 kb/d of heavy-crude demand is not back until there is public word or the weekly data shows Midwest runs recovering.
changes.conditional: Joliet confirmed → ~275 kb/d of PADD 2 heavy-crude demand back. No dollar translation: the differential model is uncalibrated pending licensed marks, so no model-implied $Y exists.
changes.source: Quantum Commodity Intelligence headlines (paywalled); ExxonMobil Sep 18 statement
changes.title: Joliet still unconfirmed — the strip's verdict

changes.balance: A settlement removes the strike wildcard; a walkout is the mirror image of Joliet — a demand step-off that widens the discount.
changes.body: The September 29 session between BP and United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 at Whiting failed: per bp's post-session statement, the union walked out without meaningfully engaging. The lockout of about 800 workers has run since March 19. The refinery is operating on replacement workers with no reported operations impact, but the strike tail stays live — a walkout would cut the single largest PADD 2 demand point for heavy sour crude.
changes.delta: Sep 29 talks failed; union walked; lockout continues
changes.title: Whiting union talks fail — lockout continues

changes.balance: The refinery war went structural: this is the supply-side leg under record global diesel cracks, and the constructive leg for synthetic crude over WCS into winter.
changes.body: Overnight strikes damaged a primary refining unit at the Moscow refinery that accounts for 53% of the plant's capacity; operations halted (Reuters, two industry sources; Zelensky confirmed a 500-km strike). Russia retaliated overnight on Kyiv (4 killed, power plants hit, jets scrambled in Romania and Poland). Russia's diesel-export ban is now expected to extend to October 31 (Vedomosti). Separately, Putin's Sep 28 decree restricts publication of Russian refinery volumes, export contract details, shipping routes, and exchange-sale volumes — track fuel shortages via satellite/transponder data, not Russian releases.
changes.delta: Moscow refinery halted (53% of capacity); diesel ban expected to Oct 31
changes.title: Moscow refinery halted overnight; Russian diesel ban expected to extend

changes.balance: The weekend's rejection premium is unwound. The curve still reads acute front tightness with normalization further out — flat-price noise for the WCS differential until it changes refinery runs or freight.
changes.body: The Saudi East-West pipeline restarted and Aramco notified customers of Yanbu Red Sea loading schedules; Saudi September crude exports hit 5.8 mb/d, the highest since February (ANZ Research). WTI Nov26 settled Tuesday at $89.38 (-3.48%), first sub-$90 print since August 31; Brent Nov26 settled $102.59 (-2.56%). Brent November expires today, with December (~$95.30) taking the front; Brent-November/December backwardation is about $7. Trump denied an Axios report he would offer Iran sanctions relief ('I offered them NOTHING'), but Iran says it received a US proposal via mediators (Tasnim, Sep 30) — the next headline risk.
changes.delta: WTI Nov $89.38 (-3.48%); Brent Nov $102.59 (-2.56%); ~$7 Nov/Dec backwardation
changes.title: Quarter-end selloff as the Saudi bypass reopens

changes.balance: Hormuz diplomacy is stalled-to-slightly-bearish on spot; the physical healing continues, offset by Houthi escalation in the Red Sea. The US diesel-export policy risk de-escalated to voluntary measures.
changes.body: Flows are healing: 13.1 mb/d through Hormuz last week, about 80% of the pre-war rate (Kpler). The counterweight: the Houthis stepped up Red Sea attacks and asserted control over Bab el-Mandeb (Wall Street Journal, Sep 30); France is deploying defensive assets to Yanbu. The diesel-export-limit policy risk de-escalated: the White House says no ban is being prepared and Energy Secretary Wright opposes a blanket ban — voluntary refiner cooperation and red-dyed diesel floated instead (RBN Energy led the story Sep 28).
changes.delta: Hormuz ~80% of pre-war; no US diesel ban in the works
changes.source: Kpler; Wall Street Journal; RBN Energy; White House
changes.title: Hormuz healing, Red Sea escalation, diesel-ban risk de-escalates

changes.balance: Bearish for Gulf Coast heavy diffs to the extent the barrels are actually taken — another length competing for the marginal coker slot alongside Merey. Watch the awards, not the RFP.
changes.body: The US Department of Energy issued a request for proposals (Sep 30) for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, continuing the 172-million-barrel coordinated release program. It is an exchange, not a sale: borrowers return the barrels plus a premium (earlier exchanges averaged ~25%). Source sites: Big Hill and Bryan Mound; deliveries November and December 2026; bids due Oct 6, 11:00 AM CT. DOE says five previous solicitations awarded 133+ million barrels across four completed exchanges. The grade slate for this tranche is not yet documented; the SPR skews sour.
changes.delta: DOE RFP: up to 40M bbl exchange, Big Hill/Bryan Mound, Nov-Dec delivery
changes.title: SPR 40-million-barrel exchange RFP lands on the USGC

changes.balance: The enforced Merey discount is the competing length against WCS for the marginal coker slot — it persists without steepening. If China-bound Merey runs stop clearing the Indian Ocean, that is supportive for WCS.
changes.body: US tanker enforcement went transoceanic: forces boarded the suezmax Aquila II in the Indian Ocean on Sep 29 — tracked from the Caribbean, ~700,000 bbl of Venezuelan heavy bound for China. First long-haul interdiction outside the Caribbean: dark-fleet runs can no longer assume safety past the Atlantic. The Sagitta was seized in the Caribbean (7th seizure); the VLCC Veronica III was boarded Sep 27; Reuters reports dozens of sealed seizure warrants in the pipeline (unconfirmed). About 20% of Venezuela's seaborne exports since December have gone to Caribbean storage, marketed by Trafigura and Vitol (Vortexa). Merey is still offered at $18-20/bbl under Brent; Jose-to-USGC Aframax freight is near $3.5 million per voyage (~$5/bbl).
changes.delta: Aquila II boarded in the Indian Ocean (700k bbl China-bound); 7th seizure
changes.title: Venezuela enforcement goes transoceanic

changes.balance: Near-term, apportionment binds: extra barrels clear through price (wider differentials), not through spare capacity. Medium-term, the TMX toll settlement locks in egress certainty from January 2027.
changes.body: Implied spare takeaway is about 272 kb/d on lagged June data — Keystone ~94% of available capacity, Mainline ~94.5%. October Mainline apportionment is binding at 8% on lights and 4% on heavies, per the Enbridge notice of Sep 16, 2026. The CER approved Trans Mountain's negotiated toll settlement Monday: contracted capacity rises from 80% to 90% of 890 kb/d from Jan 1, 2027, with an open season oversubscribed more than 2.5x and +300 kb/d via optimization by 2028. The in-house corridor model (synthetic, not observed) has Keystone and TMX at 100% across the 12-month window.
changes.source: Enbridge Connecting Pipelines notice; CER decision
changes.title: Pipes functionally full; apportionment binding

changes.balance: The 3-2-1 is not grade-specific: it says run crude, not run heavy. A wide WCS print against a strong 3-2-1 is saturated cokers choosing between WCS and Merey, not weak demand.
changes.body: Distillate is the shortage: ICE gasoil Oct26 closed Sep 29 at $1,401.75/ton (-3.1%); the US heating-oil crack peaked at $117/bbl mid-September (Bloomberg); the US diesel crack hit triple digits Monday, about $100 Tuesday; Europe diesel-over-Brent above $95/bbl — a record on 2011 data. RBN Energy's 3-2-1: $67.43 (-0.76, Sep 29); a record $75/bbl in September on the Trading Economics index. Distillate-led tightness is the engine of the synthetic-crude-versus-WCS dislocation ($27.65 on November).
changes.delta: RBN 3-2-1 $67.43 (-0.76); US diesel crack triple digits
changes.title: Record diesel complex; 3-2-1 at $67.43

changes.balance: A de-escalation headline hurts the crowded WTI longs most; fresh escalation could drive a WTI catch-up rally, since WTI lags Brent by about $13.2.
changes.body: Speculators in WTI are net long 101,828 contracts (Commodity Futures Trading Commission data as of Sep 22), the 96th percentile of the one-year range: a crowded long that would have to unwind if prices fall. In ICE Brent, speculators already washed about 23% of their length in a week (-64.5k) and are de-risked. The in-house COT model flags sub-whale commercial-sized net-short builds on the ICE WCS 1A and ICE SW 1A differentials (-5,874 and -2,259 lots) — probably trade-house hedging into the Joliet return, attribution withheld.
changes.delta: WTI 96th percentile; Brent specs washed; sub-whale shorts build on WCS/SW
changes.title: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent de-risked

changes.balance: An illustrative model read, not a live market print: while the window is open, barrels reclassify from the heavy pool into the light pool at the margin — a softener on the discount, not a directional call.
changes.body: Our blender-behavior nowcast (in-house, synthetic assumptions clearly flagged) has the heavy-into-light arbitrage window open: the viscosity constraint is binding and the incentive to blend heavy barrels into the light pool reads a net $5.51/bbl on the modeled stack, or about 43.2 kb/d of reclassification per 100 kb/d of light tendered. Direction matters, level does not.
changes.title: Blending arb window open (illustrative)

flags.body: Quantum Commodity Intelligence headlines Joliet back in service as of about Sep 28, but the article is paywalled and no public confirmation exists. ExxonMobil's last public statement (Sep 18): power restored, restart underway, no date given. The confirmation itself is the catalyst: the discount snaps tighter when it lands, stays under pressure while it does not. Today's EIA weekly (PADD 2 runs, Canadian imports) is the first public test.
flags.title: Joliet restart awaiting confirmation
flags.trigger: Public confirmation from ExxonMobil or a second source turns this into the top ranked change.
